title: Ticketing platform user and role list
what_it_shows: Two logins: the owner's administrator login and one shared 'door' login with the scanner role, created in 2024 with its password unchanged since; the scanner role can scan tickets and search orders by patron name and email; no named sub-users exist, although the platform supports them

title: Ticketing platform account security settings
what_it_shows: The administrator login signs in with a password only; MFA is available and turned off; password reset goes to the owner's business mailbox

title: Ticketing platform activity log screen and notification settings
what_it_shows: The activity log records administrator sign-ins, setting changes, exports and payout changes and keeps 90 days; each month in the period shows a full patron export by the administrator login; notification settings include a payout-change email alert

title: Ticketing platform event, ticket limit, bot protection and smart pricing settings
what_it_shows: A limit of 6 tickets per order on every event; bot protection on for every on-sale with the vendor's default settings; smart pricing in auto-apply mode on 8 shows since 2026-05-01 (5 seated, 3 standing) with no floor or ceiling prices set; seated shows carry accessible seating price levels, and no setting ties them to same-section prices

title: Ticketing platform sales and orders report, 12 months to 2026-06-30
what_it_shows: About 60 public shows (about 12 of them seated); about 6,800 tickets in about 3,600 orders, about 110 tickets per show; ticket face value about $146,000; about 120 orders entered through the box office order screen under the administrator login

title: Ticketing platform patron records summary
what_it_shows: About 14,000 patron records (buyers since 2021) holding name, email, phone, ZIP code and order history; about 85% have a Florida ZIP code; checkout requires buyers to confirm they are 18 or older

title: Ticketing platform connected apps page
what_it_shows: Two connected apps: the email marketing sync (last sync 2026-07) and a survey tool connected in 2024 with no activity since 2024

title: Payment processor portal: users, security and card volume
what_it_shows: The owner is the only portal user; the processor enforces MFA with the authenticator app on the owner's phone; transaction and chargeback screens show only the last 4 card digits; payouts settle to the business bank account two business days after each sale; 12 months to 2026-06-30: about 3,600 card orders, about 55% Visa (about 2,000); the portal states no merchant level

title: PCI compliance portal: SAQ history and notices
what_it_shows: The portal assigned SAQ A; the 2025 SAQ A was submitted on 2025-10-14 with 'yes' to every question and no attachments or scope description; a portal notice dated 2026-06-15 says the 2026 SAQ A is due 2026-10-31

title: Merchant agreement
what_it_shows: The owner is the merchant of record for ticket sales; the agreement requires compliance with the current PCI DSS and card brand rules; payouts settle two business days after each sale; the merchant must notify the processor's risk team immediately, and no later than 24 hours, after suspecting a compromise of card data

title: Website builder security settings and site code
what_it_shows: Administrator sign-in with a password only; MFA is available and turned off; event calendar pages embed the ticketing checkout widget; the site's code and plugin settings load a social media tracking pixel, a web analytics tag and a chat widget plugin on all pages, including event pages; plugins update automatically; no notes of a review of these scripts

title: Website builder security documentation
what_it_shows: The builder runs a web application firewall in front of all customer sites, patches its hosting platform, and updates plugins automatically

title: Website privacy notice, event page text and refund page
what_it_shows: The privacy notice (a 2022 template) says patron information is never shared with third parties for marketing; event pages say 'limit 6 tickets per customer'; the refund page says the service fee is not refunded unless the show is cancelled

title: Productivity suite security, sign-in and storage settings
what_it_shows: Business plan; MFA on with the authenticator app on the owner's phone; sign-in history kept; spam and phishing filtering on; file version history on; cloud storage holds artist contracts, settlement sheets and a folder of monthly patron export files from 2024-12 onward; the mailbox is the password-reset address for the other business accounts

title: Email marketing service account
what_it_shows: About 9,500 subscribers; the list is refreshed by uploading a monthly patron export; one login (the owner's), which the marketing assistant also uses

title: Accounting SaaS users and security settings
what_it_shows: Two logins: the owner's, with MFA on, and the outside bookkeeper's own login; holds vendor and artist payment details and business bank data

title: Laptop settings review
what_it_shows: Built-in full-disk encryption on; automatic updates on and update history current; built-in antivirus with real-time scanning and automatic updates; host firewall on; screen lock after 5 minutes; the owner is the local administrator; logging at default settings; time set automatically; the downloads folder holds monthly patron export files; the browser is used for the ticketing box office order screen; the laptop also joins home and public Wi-Fi networks

title: Owner's phone settings review
what_it_shows: Passcode set and device encrypted; lock after 1 minute; automatic updates on; the authenticator app holds the second factor for email, the processor portal and accounting, and it is the only registered authenticator device; no recovery codes are saved for any account; business email and text threads with fans are on the phone

title: Scanning phones settings review
what_it_shows: 2 older phones with only the scanner app installed; passcode and 1-minute lock; automatic updates on; signed in with the shared door login; kept in the office between shows

title: Walk-through of the Room and the office
source_system: The Room and office (observation, non-show day)
what_it_shows: The landlord controls the street entrance; the office behind the stage has a keyed lock and holds the 2 scanning phones and the ISP router; one Wi-Fi network name is broadcast in the Room and its password is on a sign backstage; the laptop and scanning phones are joined to it, and the owner states the sound engineer and touring crews use the same network; the owner states no router setting has been changed since the ISP installed it; no paper with card data in the office

title: Lease of the Room
what_it_shows: 5-year lease of the Room, a 280-person standing room (150 seated in cabaret layout) on the ground floor of a mixed-use building, with an office behind the stage; the landlord owns the building and controls the street entrance, the fire alarm, and the building's internet service to the Room

title: Contractor agreements and engagement records
what_it_shows: Door and security contractor: service agreement for 2 to 3 door and security staff per show, with no data, confidentiality or incident notice terms; outside bookkeeper: engagement letter for quarterly bookkeeping and tax filings; on-call IT consultant: confidentiality agreement signed 2026-07-24; marketing assistant (about 10 hours a week) and sound engineer: engaged verbally, with no written terms

title: Bank and card statements, 2025-07-01 to 2026-07-17
source_system: Business bank account and card statements
what_it_shows: Recurring charges for the website builder, productivity suite, email marketing service and accounting SaaS; payments to the door and security contractor, marketing assistant, sound engineer, outside bookkeeper and IT consultant (hourly); lease and general liability premium payments; deposits from processor payouts, the bar concessionaire's revenue share, rental fees and sponsorship; no payment for a cyber insurance policy; no payment to any AI tool provider

title: 2025 Schedule C (Form 1040)
source_system: Owner's tax files (prepared with the outside bookkeeper)
what_it_shows: Gross receipts of about $180,000; no wages paid; the business is a sole proprietorship with no employees

title: Income by category, 2025
what_it_shows: Ticket face value about $146,000; bar concessionaire revenue share about $19,000; private rentals about $11,000 (about 15 rentals); sponsorship about $4,000

title: Bar concession agreement and 2025 revenue share statements
what_it_shows: The concessionaire runs the bar under its own liquor license, staff, POS and merchant account and pays the owner a revenue share (about $19,000 in 2025)

title: Search of the owner's files for security and PCI DSS documents
source_system: Laptop; cloud storage; email; paper files in the office
what_it_shows: No written security policy or procedure, risk assessment, incident plan or contact list, PCI DSS scope description, list of service providers, vendor AOC, retention rule, security training record, or stored recovery codes was found

title: Owner's written intake account of sales, accounts and records
what_it_shows: Phone orders: the owner keys the caller's card number into the box office order screen in the laptop browser while the caller waits, and nothing is written down; some fans send card details by email or text for the owner to key in the same way; the marketing assistant signs in with the owner's ticketing, website and email marketing logins; the ticketing and website logins use the same password; the owner has not reviewed the ticketing activity log, payout changes or website changes; patron exports are downloaded each month and kept on the laptop and in cloud storage for the assistant, with no rule on how long; the 2025 SAQ A answers were given without a separate check of the eligibility criteria; smart pricing was turned on after a vendor webinar without a review of total-price display, artist price caps or accessible seating prices; the owner has had no security training

title: Business social posts and flyer files, 2026
source_system: Business social media accounts (SYS-05); flyer files in cloud storage
what_it_shows: 2026 posts and flyers state ticket prices in the form '$X plus fees'; the flyer template prints the face price in large type; the ticketing platform's event pages show the total price

title: General liability policy declarations
what_it_shows: General liability coverage for events in force for 2026; the declarations page lists no cyber or data breach coverage; the full policy form was requested from the agent

title: Ticketing vendor SOC 2 Type 2 report
source_system: Ticketing platform vendor (provided under a nondisclosure agreement)
what_it_shows: Type 2 report on the Security and Availability categories for the 12 months ending 2026-03-31; the system description states RTO 4 hours and near-zero RPO and describes backups of orders, payments and patron records; MFA is offered to customers and not enforced by default; lists complementary user entity controls; the payment processor and hosting provider are carved-out subservice organizations

title: Ticketing platform product documentation
what_it_shows: The payment fields in the hosted checkout and the embeddable widget are served by the processor; named sub-users with roles are supported; the activity log keeps 90 days; the scanner app works offline with the attendee list downloaded before doors; smart pricing uses sales velocity, tickets remaining, days to the show, page views and the owner's price settings, and per the vendor no patron-level data; bot protection scores sessions on device, browser, network and timing signals

title: Marketing assistant's answers on tools and accounts
what_it_shows: Uses a consumer generative AI chatbot on a free plan to draft show descriptions and posts; posts from the business social accounts with the owner's login on the assistant's phone; signs in to the ticketing platform, the website and the email marketing service with the owner's logins; uploads the monthly patron export to the email marketing service; uses no other AI tool

title: BIA worksheet
source_system: Owner's written BIA worksheet, reviewed with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: For each of the five business functions, the owner's account of the systems and vendors used, the manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss the function can tolerate; an outage of more than 2 hours on an on-sale day loses most first-day sales; the owner is the only person who can run settlement, the guest list, pricing, payouts, refunds and the processor portal

title: Risk walk-through of accounts, devices and the Room's network
source_system: Walk-through of every SaaS account, the laptop, the phones and the router with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: Where patron and card data end up (exports on the laptop and in cloud storage, the email marketing service, the mailbox, phone texts, phone orders keyed on the laptop); artist deposits and settlements are paid to bank details received by email with no call-back; the business runs from a single room with shows booked weeks ahead; every second factor is on the owner's phone

title: General liability policy form
what_it_shows: The general liability policy excludes data breach costs

title: Smart pricing price change history, 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-31
what_it_shows: 37 price changes on 8 shows (5 seated, 3 standing); on 1 show the price exceeded the artist's agreed cap by 12% for 4 days; accessible seating stayed at or below same-section prices on all 5 seated shows

title: Gap analysis self-review
source_system: Owner's written answers to the PCI DSS, FTC and Florida questions, checked on screen with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: No written procedures for network rules, configuration, malware protection, changes, access, authentication, physical access, logging or security testing; no rule on what card data may be received, kept or sent by message; no scans of any kind; nobody checks the event pages for new or changed scripts; nobody reviews the ticketing activity log, website changes or email sign-ins

title: Browser capture of the event pages
source_system: Website event pages (SYS-03), browser developer tools
what_it_shows: Event pages load the checkout widget together with the social media pixel, the analytics tag and the chat widget code; the pixel sends event page visits and checkout starts to the social platform; the chat widget plugin can add code to every page, including event pages

title: Card number search of the mailbox, phone, laptop and cloud storage
source_system: Mailbox and cloud storage (SYS-04); owner's phone and laptop (SYS-07)
what_it_shows: 23 emails (2023 to 2026) and 4 text messages from fans held full card numbers, 19 of the emails with the security code; no card numbers in files on the laptop or in cloud storage; numbers were counted, not copied

title: Card data deletion record
what_it_shows: The 23 emails and 4 text messages holding card numbers were deleted from all folders, including trash

title: Patron export folder review and cloud storage sharing report
source_system: Laptop downloads folder (SYS-07); cloud storage sharing report (SYS-04)
what_it_shows: 19 monthly patron exports (2024-12 to 2026-07) on the laptop and in cloud storage; 4 export files in cloud storage had 'anyone with the link' sharing, created for the marketing assistant; the owner turned the links off the same day

title: Checkout, order screen and portal screenshots
source_system: Ticketing checkout and order screens (SYS-01); processor portal (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: Ticketing order screens and the processor portal show only the last 4 card digits to every role; the checkout shows the total price, itemizes the service fee by name and shows the final amount before payment

what_it_shows: Service provider AOC dated 2026-03-12 covering the platform and its hosted checkout

title: Payment processor PCI DSS attestation of compliance
what_it_shows: Service provider AOC dated 2026-01-30 covering card processing and the payment fields in the hosted checkout

title: Review of 2026 social posts and flyers
source_system: Business social accounts (SYS-05); flyer files in cloud storage
what_it_shows: 17 of 20 sampled 2026 social posts and all 6 2026 flyers show '$X plus fees' without the total price; the flyers print the face price in large type and 'plus fees' in small type

title: Merchant agreement review
source_system: Merchant agreement, read with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: The agreement requires notice to the processor's risk team immediately, and no later than 24 hours, after the merchant suspects a compromise of card data; the owner had not been aware of this term

title: Show-night walk-through of the Room
source_system: The Room and office (observation during a show)
what_it_shows: Crew and artist devices joined the same Wi-Fi network as the laptop and scanning phones; the Wi-Fi password on the backstage sign has not changed since 2024; crews brought their own access points and nobody checked them; the office stayed locked and crews and contractors were kept out of it; the landlord's staff controlled the street entrance

title: Bot protection on-sale reports and fan emails
source_system: Ticketing platform bot protection reports (SYS-01); mailbox (SYS-04)
what_it_shows: On the 2 sold-out on-sales of 2026 bot protection blocked 610 sessions; the vendor report shows totals only; 3 fans emailed that they were blocked; the only route to appeal is emailing the owner

title: Chatbot history review with the marketing assistant
what_it_shows: The history held show descriptions and post drafts; one conversation from 2026-06 contained a pasted patron complaint email with the patron's name and email; the assistant deleted that conversation on 2026-08-12

title: Control assessment: Risk assessment review
source_system: P01 risk register; P05 BIA; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The 2026 risk assessment identifies 15 threat events with sources and vulnerabilities, rates likelihood and impact with Tables G-5 and I-2, includes harm to patrons, takes the business view from the BIA, and is documented in the register and report; results were shared with the IT consultant under the confidentiality agreement; no review frequency or update trigger was defined at the time of assessment

title: Control assessment: Administrator sign-in tests
source_system: Account security pages; sign-in tests from a new browser
what_it_shows: Email, processor portal and accounting sign-ins required the authenticator app; the ticketing platform and website administrator logins signed in with a password only

title: Control assessment: Password and default credential tests
source_system: Ticketing, website and router credentials; door login history; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The ticketing platform and website accept the same password, which the marketing assistant also uses, and the owner sent it to the assistant by text; the door login password was set by the owner in 2024, is short, was sent by text to the door contractor's lead with no check of who received it, and was not changed as door staff changed; the router accepted its default administrator password, and the owner changed it during the test; no written procedure for issuing, replacing or revoking passwords and no written duty for contractors to protect them; the authenticator app sits on the passcode-locked phone and the laptop password store behind the encrypted device login

title: Control assessment: Provider and contractor review
source_system: Vendor AOCs; vendor terms; contractor arrangements; website and ticketing user and connected-app lists
what_it_shows: Ticketing vendor and processor AOCs are dated 2026 and were first obtained on 2026-07-28; no written security, privacy or confidentiality terms with the marketing assistant or the door contractor; no provider list or oversight steps documented; the merchant agreement and the ticketing vendor's terms assign responsibility for the card data each provider handles, and the vendor's SOC 2 report lists customer responsibilities; the website builder's administrator list still included a former freelance assistant engaged until 2025-11, removed by the owner during the test; the unused 2024 survey tool was removed from the ticketing platform's connected apps the same day

title: Control assessment: Card data and patron export review
source_system: Mailbox, phone, laptop and cloud storage search; export folder; sharing report
what_it_shows: The 2026-07-28 search, repeated on the laptop on 2026-07-29, found card numbers in 23 emails and 4 texts (19 with security codes) and none in laptop files or cloud storage; 19 monthly patron exports on the laptop and in cloud storage; 4 export files had 'anyone with the link' sharing (turned off 2026-07-28); no retention rule for records holding patron data

title: Control assessment: Activity review and payout alert test
source_system: Ticketing activity log; website change history; email sign-in history; payout-change test; owner self-review
what_it_shows: No record of any review of the ticketing activity log, website change history or email sign-ins; the payout-change test sent the alert only to the account email (the owner's); no process to act on review results or to increase review around on-sales or after an incident or vendor notice

title: Control assessment: Incident reporting self-review
source_system: Merchant agreement; contractor arrangements; owner self-review
what_it_shows: No reporting time for contractors; the owner had not known the processor's 24-hour notice term; no list of whom to notify (processor, ticketing vendor, counsel, law enforcement, the Florida Department of Legal Affairs)

title: Control assessment: Backup review
source_system: Ticketing vendor SOC 2 report; cloud storage version history settings
what_it_shows: The SOC 2 report shows the vendor backs up orders, payments, patron records and the platform, encrypts backups, checks their integrity and keeps them in a separate location, with no exceptions on these controls; business files and security documents are in cloud storage with version history on

title: Control assessment: Router and network review
source_system: Router settings and firewall; Wi-Fi network list; show-night walk-through
what_it_shows: The router firewall denies unsolicited inbound connections (checked 2026-07-29); the router keeps no logs the owner can read; one Wi-Fi network serves the laptop, scanning phones, crews and artists, with no guest network and no monitoring inside it (show night 2026-07-30); all traffic leaves through the router and the office has no other internet connection
